changelog:
- Expanded French, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Russian UI dictionaries with 58 shared labels per locale for Extensions, Capability Center, common actions, welcome and browser connection states; expanded ROM Builder page-specific translations across all six non-English locales.
- Refactored ROM Builder's Agent control CLI to version 3: direct `control read`, `control set`, and `control press` operations now mirror visible GUI controls, while `snapshot` exposes shared form, job, terminal, sensor, and error state. Legacy CLI commands remain compatible.
- Expanded ROM Builder trigger routing to recognize Android ROM build intent (LineageOS, AOSP, repo sync, lunch/brunch, GApps, device codenames, clean and upload requests) even when the product name is not repeated.
- Added dedicated read-only ROM Builder module and writable shared-state mounts for the Agent runtime. The launcher exports the mount paths and the host UI/backend share the same `logs/rom-builder-state` directory.
- Updated the ROM Builder add-on manifest to normalized ID `rom-builder`, version 1.6, and synchronized its control skill into both app skill locations.
- Added installed-module discovery for Ghidra MCP Server and a non-navigating, disabled sidebar entry labeled “Ghidra MCP Server” with an Installed indicator. The entry appears only when the Ghidra module manifest and installer script are present.
- Unified `/modules` and `/api/modules` discovery so the workspace sidebar and ROM Builder page use the same installed add-on inventory.
- Added localized Add-on Tools, ROM Builder, Ghidra MCP Server, and Installed sidebar labels for English, Chinese, French, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, and Russian.
- Added the `rom-builder-control` skill and mirrored it into the runtime skill view. The skill follows the Ghidra-style control workflow: inspect the CLI, discover the GUI control specification, snapshot current state, operate only documented controls, and verify changes. Expanded ROM Builder trigger routing for ROM Builder, Android, LineageOS, and AOSP build requests.
- Translation coverage after this batch: 25.9% average across the six non-English locales (key-level coverage against 1,794 English UI string entries; Chinese 100%, French/Japanese/Korean/Portuguese/Russian approximately 11.0% each). Added 58 shared UI labels per non-Chinese locale across Extensions, Capability Center, common, welcome and browser connection states, plus eight additional ROM Builder page messages per locale. This measures translated string keys, not visual area or user traffic.
- Fixed the Ghidra sandbox mount startup failure: config resolution accepts only whole-value `$VARIABLE` references, so the launcher now exports `ATEAM_GHIDRA_MODULE_DIR` as the exact add-on directory and config mounts it read-only at `/mnt/ateam-ghidra-module`. Both copies of the Ghidra setup skill now stage from that mounted path, avoiding unsupported variable suffix interpolation and avoiding exposure of the full application root.
- Exported the canonical installed application directory as `ATEAM_PROJECT_ROOT` from the launcher after environment/profile loading, making the Ghidra setup skill resolve `modules/Ghidra-MCP-Server` without a hardcoded host path; left `DEER_FLOW_PROJECT_ROOT` unchanged to preserve backend runtime path semantics.
- Corrected Ghidra skill staging to resolve the A-Team application root from `ATEAM_PROJECT_ROOT` or `DEER_FLOW_PROJECT_ROOT`, then append `modules/Ghidra-MCP-Server`; removed all personal home-directory paths and the unsafe `$PWD` fallback. The skill copies the module into `/mnt/user-data/workspace/modules/Ghidra-MCP-Server` at invocation time and verifies `ghidra.py`.
- Moved Ghidra source staging out of the launcher and into the Ghidra setup skill, which resolves the installed add-on at skill runtime and copies its source into the canonical workspace; installing the add-on no longer requires an agent restart.
- Added the root `versions.json` add-on catalog with the supplied `addon_1_*` ROM Builder and `addon_2_*` Ghidra MCP Server entries; the Tool Add-Ons pane reads these numbered entries from the configured GitHub modules branch.
- Documented `ATEAM_MODULE_REPO_OWNER`, `ATEAM_MODULE_REPO_NAME`, and `ATEAM_MODULE_REPO_BRANCH` in `frontend/.env.example` so the add-on repository and branch can be configured without editing source.
- Updated the Add-Ons pane description to identify `versions.json` as the versioned catalog source.
- Hardened add-on ZIP installation for module upgrades: an existing module may be atomically replaced only when the incoming and installed `module.json` IDs match (ROM Builder retains its dedicated upgrade flow); failed replacements restore the prior module.
- Normalized extracted add-on script permissions: `.sh` entrypoints are `755`; Python, docs, config and source files remain `644`.
- Kept launcher workspace provisioning separate from module staging; the Ghidra skill now copies only the installer and metadata from the live add-on at execution time, preserving the runtime, downloads, and virtual environment.
- Updated Ghidra skill bootstrap to check known application-root `modules/` locations at execution time, copy the installed add-on source into the workspace, verify the copy, and fail with a mount-specific diagnostic if the application module directory is not exposed.
- Updated the Ghidra module README with the skill-time module staging contract and the agent-visible setup path.
- Changed the Linux launcher terminal wrappers so Ctrl+C runs the existing cleanup handler and then closes the terminal emulator instead of leaving an idle interactive shell; removed XFCE terminal hold behavior as well.
- Preserved the Ghidra setup trigger behavior; this update changes workspace provisioning and terminal shutdown, not trigger matching.
- Expanded the public `ghidra-reverse-engineering` skill into an agent-driven first-time setup procedure. When asked to set up Ghidra, the agent is instructed to run the module installer and launcher, pause for the user's native GUI action to enable `GhidraMCPPlugin`, verify the local service with `status`, register the bridge with `configure-mcp`, and explain the final A-Team tool-session reload and first analysis steps.
- Expanded `modules/Ghidra/README.md` with the complete install → launch → enable GUI plugin → status → configure MCP sequence, Java 21/Python 3.10+ prerequisites, the approximately 570 MB download/disk-space expectation, OS launcher notes, and explicit failure/verification criteria.
- Strengthened the Ghidra skill's mandatory permission rule: inspect script permissions before execution, keep Python source and skill files non-executable, invoke module scripts through Python, and permit executable-bit changes only for the verified vendor Ghidra launcher when required by Unix.
- Landing page wallpaper isolation: the global animated wallpaper is now disabled on `/` so it cannot overlap or compete with the landing page's own hero animation. The wallpaper canvas, CSS body layer and Odysseus animation loops are cleaned up on entry; the selected wallpaper preference is preserved and resumes on workspace pages.
- Added the first-party A-Team Ghidra module at `modules/Ghidra/`. It installs the full Ghidra 12.1.4 desktop distribution inside the module runtime directory, installs the matching GhidraMCP 7.0.0 GUI extension into Ghidra's per-user extension profile, creates an isolated Python bridge environment, launches the native GUI, checks the local MCP endpoint, and registers the stdio bridge in `extensions_config.json`.
- Ghidra setup pins official upstream release URLs and SHA-256 digests for the Ghidra distribution, GhidraMCP extension ZIP and Python wheel. The installer verifies all downloads before extraction, rejects ZIP path traversal, keeps third-party binaries out of the source archive, and creates a one-time backup before editing an existing MCP config. The module includes setup/launch/status/configure/disable commands and upstream/license notes.
- Added the public `ghidra-reverse-engineering` skill under `skills/public/` (and its runtime skill-view mirror). It documents installation, launch, MCP setup, analysis workflow, evidence reporting, authorization boundaries and mandatory script-permission review. Ghidra script execution remains disabled by default (`GHIDRA_MCP_ALLOW_SCRIPTS=0`).
- Wallpaper rendering: Ember particles now parse the configured effect color once per frame instead of once for each particle/gradient stop, and reuse a cached white RGB constant for highlights.
- High-priority dialog hardening: ordinary dialogs now receive a fixed, viewport-based position with important inline positioning and centering, recalculated after open, resize, and content-size changes. Full-viewport settings dialogs and intentionally anchored Create Project dialogs retain their bespoke layouts.
- Removed the broad wallpaper rule that positioned arbitrary direct children of `<body>`. Only workspace content surfaces are raised above the background canvas, leaving Radix portal roots and popup windows outside the wallpaper stacking/containing-block rules.
- Renamed Appearance → App Transparency to App Opacity; renamed Main chat transparency and ROM Builder transparency to Main Chat Opacity and ROM Builder Opacity. Added Transparent/Solid slider endpoint labels. All three opacity controls now default to `0` (fully transparent) and retain individual browser-stored values.
- Changed Capability Center opacity default from `100` to `0`; the saved value still applies live to the Capability Center surface and cards.
- Added localized App Opacity labels, descriptions and slider endpoints to all seven shipped locales (English, Simplified Chinese, French, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Russian).
- Reviewed Ghidra MCP integration: the target is a separate Ghidra GUI extension plus Python MCP bridge, not a web-renderable MCP tool. The feasible approach is a managed local bridge connection plus a browser-native reverse-engineering workspace; the native Ghidra Swing GUI should remain a separate application window.
- Fixed every shared popup (for example Delete project) opening too low and mostly off-screen. Root cause: the wallpaper stylesheet forced `position: relative` on every direct child of `<body>`, which includes the dialog portals, so it overrode the dialogs' `position: fixed` and dropped them below the page. The rule now lifts only the app shell and leaves dialogs, overlays, sheets, popovers, tooltips and toasts alone.
- Fixed the shared dialog's centering code never running: it looked up the dialog element in a plain ref inside an effect that ran while the dialog was still closed (Radix mounts the content only when open), so the element was always null. It now tracks the element with a callback ref and centers every dialog horizontally between the sidebar and the right edge of the chat pane and vertically in the window, clamped so the whole dialog stays on screen. Height capping and scrolling moved into the base classes, and dialogs that supply their own overflow behavior keep it.
- Removed the hard-coded `left: 62.5vw; top: 50dvh` placement from the Model and Sub-agent settings dialogs so they use the same exact centering as every other popup.
- Fixed the GitHub icon in the top app bar (visible on Workspace, Trash and the other workspace pages) opening a new instance of the Agent (`href="/"`); it now opens the A-Team Agent GitHub page, https://github.com/PizzaG/A-Team_Agent/, in a new tab.
- Added a Capability Center transparency slider to Appearance → App Transparency, alongside Main chat and ROM Builder. It works the same way as the existing sliders (saved per browser, applied on entering the page and live while dragging) and affects the Capability Center page background and its capability cards. It defaults to 100 so the page looks unchanged until the slider is moved.
- Fixed a wallpaper animation leak: every Intensity, Particle size or Animation speed change recreated the wallpaper canvas but left the previous animation loop running against the detached canvas, so each slider tick added another background loop and resize listener for most effects. All effects now schedule frames and resize handlers through a shared lifecycle guard that stops the previous loops and listeners whenever the wallpaper is applied or cleaned up.
- Wallpaper performance: effect speed, size and intensity are cached instead of calling `getComputedStyle()` per particle per frame; canvas resolution is capped at 1.5x instead of 2x; resize events are coalesced to one per animation frame; the Dots wallpaper is painted once (and on resize or setting change) instead of redrawing its whole grid 60 times a second; the wallpaper canvas stays 1x1 when it has nothing to draw; and the full-screen GPU-promoted `body::before` layer is created only for the four CSS wallpapers (Aurora, Waves, Vortex, Starfield) rather than for every wallpaper mode including None.
- Removed unreachable draw branches from the wallpaper canvas component (every effect it handled is drawn by the Odysseus engine) and made the first-load and change-event defaults for intensity, size and speed identical (they previously differed, so the first settings change could jump the effect).
- Build Console and ROM Builder polling: the interactive shell poll (350 ms) now pauses while the tab is hidden, never stacks overlapping requests when the server is slow, and retains at most the last 300,000 characters like the build log; the Agent status poll also pauses while the tab is hidden.
- Fixed `?settings=addons` deep links being ignored (the Add-Ons section was missing from the deep-link table) and a TypeScript error in the Add-Ons module-ZIP installer that would fail a production type-check.
- Center all shared dialog windows within the chat workspace (between the chat pane and sidebar), clamp their height to the viewport, and preserve explicit custom positioning for project dialogs. This prevents tall confirmation dialogs from opening off-screen.
- Added administrator-controlled follow-up suggestion settings in Appearance → Chat Settings, persisted to `config.yaml`; suggestions default to disabled and the maximum defaults to two (range 1–5).
- Set the frontend suggestions fallback and shipped `config.yaml` default to disabled with a maximum of two suggestions.
- Corrected the workspace GitHub menu item to use Radix `asChild` with a direct external anchor to the canonical A-Team Agent repository, avoiding nested interactive elements.
- Added localized labels and help text for suggestion settings across all seven supported locales.
- Avoided an unnecessary animation-frame loop when wallpapers are disabled or reduced-motion is requested.
- Added a cinematic Matrix Rain wallpaper with cascading Japanese/alphanumeric glyph streams, bright leading characters and fading phosphor trails. It is selectable in Appearance and uses the existing Effect color, Intensity, Particle size and Animation speed controls.
- Restored the Token Usage dropdown's output-speed row as a live, once-per-second average when incremental output-token usage is available; completed speed now uses only the current assistant turn instead of accumulated conversation output tokens. The display uses reported token usage rather than estimating tokens from streamed characters.
- Added project-context admission diagnostics that record thread/project membership, owner-scoped project lookup outcomes, instruction length, shelf counts, and whether the project block is actually injected into each model request. Logs avoid recording instruction contents, making missing project context traceable without exposing project text.
- Expanded `~` in configured sandbox mount host paths before absolute-path validation, so valid home-relative mounts such as `~/Deerflow-Work` are no longer silently skipped.
- Fixed unmanaged Ollama detection by resolving the process that owns the configured API listener (via `/proc` socket inodes, with `lsof`/`fuser` fallback) instead of requiring an exact `ollama serve` argv shape. Supports symlinked executables and wrapped/desktop-launched Ollama processes, reports listener executable/command details when ownership is ambiguous, and still refuses to terminate non-Ollama listeners, multiple candidates, or daemons owned by another user.
- Fixed systemd Ollama detection to use the loaded-unit state and active service status, with canonical unit-file fallbacks, instead of relying on `systemctl cat` succeeding. This recognizes the existing `/etc/systemd/system/ollama.service` installation and its VRAM drop-ins, routes setup through the service configuration/restart path, and avoids the unmanaged-listener scanner for systemd-owned Ollama. Service snapshots also fall back to privileged unit inspection when needed.
- Fixed VRAM setup for an already-running user-managed Ollama daemon: the setup snapshots its effective environment, identifies and gracefully stops the exact local `ollama serve` process owned by the current user, relaunches it with the selected 800 MiB GPU policy and preserved non-conflicting settings, and verifies the existing model tags before saving setup state. Unidentified, multi-process, supervisor-restarted, or other-user daemons are left untouched with actionable diagnostics. Bumped the VRAM setup record to schema 5 so installations from the previous package rerun setup.
- Increased the Ollama GPU scheduler safety margin from 400 MiB to 800 MiB per GPU for GPU-backed policies, updated the Resource Monitor and Agent sensor reporting, and bumped the VRAM setup record to schema 4 so existing schema-3 installations rerun setup and apply the larger reserve before Agent startup.
- Removed the Build Console's artificial blank-line gap and “Press ENTER to Exit” prompt; after a task completes, the persistent interactive terminal remains at the loaded ROM source root without requiring a synthetic exit step.
- Reworked Build Configuration into the exact three-row control layout beneath Android source directory: Device/GApps variant/Installer variant; Android version/Custom APN/Use ccache; Build variant/Build jobs/Clean variant/Known ROM build command. Reduced both switch-card widths equally, narrowed Build jobs, and left all action buttons unchanged.
- Aligned the CPU and GPU model-name headers in the same responsive row whenever Resource Monitor uses its side-by-side layout.
- Corrected the bundled ROM Builder skill's YAML frontmatter (the unquoted colon in its description made the YAML invalid), added valid metadata, and publish it into DeerFlow's configured `skills/public/` source directory rather than the unused runtime skills path. Module install/reinstall and uninstall now request the Gateway skill-cache reload and clean up the legacy misplaced copy, so the skill is available only while ROM Builder is installed.
- Expanded the Ollama first-run setup to take a private pre-change snapshot of the installed Ollama version, effective systemd environment, service unit, server.json settings, API-visible models, and all discovered model-store locations. It checks the official latest Ollama release and offers an opt-in Linux update before applying the selected memory policy.
- Preserved non-conflicting Ollama, runner, and proxy environment settings when rebuilding the systemd override; reconnected the previously discovered model manifests and blobs through the selected OLLAMA_MODELS store, then verified model visibility after the service restart.
- Added a third Ollama memory policy, CPU/RAM-only: CUDA and ROCm devices are hidden from the Ollama daemon, ChatOllama requests set num_gpu=0, and GPU scheduler reservation is disabled for this mode. Existing GPU-only and GPU-first-with-spillover choices remain available.
- Added a required first-run Ollama VRAM Usage Setup with persistent setup state. The launcher checks the setup record before starting the Agent and runs the setup wizard when it is absent; an explicit reconfigure flag reruns the wizard and backs up the previous record.
- Expanded Ollama first-run setup to inventory existing model stores before changing the daemon, including `~/.ollama/models`, `/home/*/.ollama/models`, common system/service directories, configured `OLLAMA_MODELS`, and the existing systemd service path. It reconnects model manifests and content-addressed blobs without re-downloading large model files, grants service-user access with ACLs while preserving ownership, configures `OLLAMA_MODELS`, and verifies that previously discovered model tags remain visible through `ollama list` before saving setup state or starting the Agent.
- Added a launcher model-store preflight: saved VRAM setup records must use the verified model-store schema, the selected `OLLAMA_MODELS` directory is restored on launch, and the Agent is blocked if models discovered during setup disappear from Ollama's model list.
- Added two Ollama memory policies: GPU-only mode reserves 400 MiB per GPU, disables automatic memory fitting, and requests all model layers on the GPU; GPU-first mode reserves the same margin while retaining Ollama CPU/RAM spillover for models that exceed available VRAM. Systemd-managed Ollama services receive and verify the selected environment settings before the setup record is written.
- Added explicit Agent ROM Builder intent triggers for “ROM-Builder”, “rom builder”, and “build a rom”; the Agent now treats these as requests to use the ROM Builder UI/CLI and inspect its controls, commands, job state, shell state, logs, prompts, and sensors.
- Added a two-line completion gap and “Press ENTER to Exit” prompt to the Build Console after a task finishes; pressing Enter returns interaction to the persistent shell in the loaded ROM source directory.
- Reserved 400 MiB of reported usable VRAM on every detected GPU for the host OS, consistently across the Resource Monitor and Agent sensor output.
- Updated the landing-page Agent Skills animation to use `/LineageOS/24.0/`, show LineageOS device/vendor/kernel files on the left, and Android ROM build activity on the right.
- Reorganized Build Configuration into the requested three rows beneath the Android source directory: Device/GApps variant/Installer variant; Android version/Custom APN/Use ccache; Build variant/Known ROM build command/Build jobs/Clean variant. Existing action buttons are unchanged.
- Fixed job discovery so persistent Build Console shell sessions are excluded from build-job polling, Agent Integration's active-task status, start-task locking, and shutdown handling.
- Fixed ROM Builder start validation so the UI's supported build-job range (1–128) is accepted consistently, and surfaced the CLI's actual validation error instead of a generic process-failed message.
- Added a persistent interactive Build Console shell that starts in the loaded Android ROM source directory and remains available outside active build tasks.
- Moved the Clean variant dropdown between Android version and GApps variant in Build Configuration.
- Removed the GPU label above the GPU model and centered the GPU model to mirror the CPU model.
- After uninstalling a module, redirect to New Chat on refresh when the removed module was the page being viewed.
- Made the Build Console terminal available after Load Configuration and updated its instructions to reflect the loaded-configuration workflow.
- Repositioned the Use ccache switch alongside Custom APN, compacted the ROM Builder action buttons, and moved GApps and Installer variants directly below Android version.
- Removed the obsolete ROM Builder updater notice from Agent Integration.
- Removed the GPU model from the GPU Temp tile and centered CPU details with the GPU model displayed alongside them.
- Updated Color Themes to match the Language selector width and open upward with the full list visible when screen space permits.
- Added an automatic page refresh after successful Tool Add-On installation or removal.
- Removed the obsolete btop Resource Monitor API route; the Resource Monitor uses the custom sensor pane.
- Updated the ROM Builder module version to 1.4.
- Reworked the ROM Builder Resource Monitor into a custom pane showing CPU temperature, usage and speed, RAM usage, GPU temperature, usage and speed, VRAM usage, and the physical core and logical thread counts (like the Windows Task Manager). Readings come from `/proc` and `/sys`, plus `nvidia-smi` and `lspci` when present; the btop terminal is no longer used by the pane.
- Added `scripts/install-sensors.sh`, a distro-aware optional helper (apt, dnf, pacman, zypper, apk, xbps) that offers to install `lm-sensors` and `pciutils` when CPU temperature is not readable. The launcher runs it once, only at a terminal and never on an update restart; `ATEAM_SKIP_SENSOR_SETUP=1` disables it.
- Added a Refresh Page icon to the top app bar, to the left of the existing right-side icon.
- Moved the Clean button to the right end of the Build Configuration action buttons.
- Removed the Send Input section from the Build Console and made the console terminal fully interactive: tasks now run in a pseudo-terminal, so keys typed in the console (Enter, arrows, Tab, Ctrl+C) go straight to the running task, and output renders colours, carriage returns and backspaces.
- Fixed the Use ccache switch stretching taller than Custom APN so both now share the same height and padding.
- Expanded the ROM Builder CLI so the Agent can run the whole app: `spec` (every control, button and output), `snapshot` (form, run readiness, jobs, console tail, sensors), `form-get`, `form-set`, `load-config`, `run`, `sensors`, `keys`, `input --raw`, `poll`, and byte-offset `logs` with `--clean`. The Build Configuration form is now shared between the web UI and the Agent, tasks the Agent starts appear in the Build Console, and a new `rom-builder-control` skill documents every command.
- Fixed the ROM Builder CLI and web UI using different state directories, which hid UI jobs from the Agent, and made the CLI mark jobs whose worker died as failed instead of blocking new tasks forever. ROM Builder module version 1.3.
- Translated the core interface (common actions, sidebar, welcome, workspace menu, conversation, shortcuts, model picker, sign-in, theme and language settings) for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Russian through a new locale merge helper; untranslated strings fall back to English. Extended the ROM Builder page translations to cover the new Resource Monitor and console text.
- Made the Language dropdown open upward with every language visible and no scrolling.
- Centered both New Project dialogs horizontally between the sidebar and the chat pane by computing their position from the measured dialog width; the dialogs' forced `translate-x-0` had been overriding the inline centering offset. Vertical placement is unchanged.
- Made `btop` the default Resource Monitor command (falling back to `btop++`, `bpytop`, then `top`), replaced a stale `btop++` session left by an earlier build, and stopped the monitor refresh from starting a login shell on every poll.
- Fixed Tool Add-Ons showing “Unknown” module versions when the repository `versions.json` has a trailing comma by parsing it leniently, and accepted numeric `version` values in installed `module.json` files.
- Fixed the ROM Builder Build Configuration resetting after navigating to chat and back during a running task: the saved configuration is now restored before any form values are saved.
- Restructured the startup output into consistent sections: “Starting Up”, “Running Dependency Checks” (checks listed first, results grouped below), “Running Startup Services”, “Starting A-Team Agent” (services, routing and logs listed before the service start lines), and a final “A-Team Agent Is Running!” summary with the connection profile, workspace and app launch note.
- Removed duplicated startup lines (connection profile and the Ctrl+C notice), silenced the uv virtual-environment and build messages during the config check, and aligned cleanup and config messages to the same `-` and `✓` style.
- Added a shared guard for the ROM Builder, add-on install and update install API routes that rejects unknown Host headers (DNS rebinding), cross-origin and cross-site requests, and requires a signed-in session when the app is reachable beyond loopback (remote connection profile). Additional trusted hostnames can be set with `ATEAM_ALLOWED_HOSTS`; `ATEAM_API_GUARD=off` disables the guard.
- Repositioned both New Project dialogs to center over the chat workspace and sit above the welcome greeting; corrected dialog measurement and transform conflicts, including when ROM Builder is loaded.
- Preserved the selected Known ROM build command when loading configuration, matching configured command IDs and values without silently resetting to Default.
- Made the in-app Resource Monitor keyboard-interactive by forwarding safe key presses to its persistent tmux session and refreshing the captured terminal view more frequently.
- Added Build Console standard-input forwarding so a running ROM Builder task can receive typed responses to interactive prompts.
- Streamlined startup dependency-check output, separated dependency checks from service startup, and removed redundant startup guidance from the automatic launch path.
- Reverted the New Project popup repositioning experiment and disabled the New Project action while ROM Builder is the selected add-on.
- Initialized ROM Builder transparency from saved local settings immediately on page load, without requiring the Appearance settings pane to open.
- Resource Monitor now prefers `btop++`, falls back to `btop`, then `bpytop` and `top`.
- Persisted Build Configuration fields locally so navigating away from ROM Builder and returning restores the current configuration while builds continue.
- Updated the Agent Integration description to “The Agent can control the workflow and run the bundled ROM Builder scripts.”
- Made Tool Add-Ons discovery find `versions.json` wherever it appears in the modules branch tree, support multiple numbered add-ons, normalize ZIP filename matching, and accept numeric or string version values.
- Updated the welcome message to the requested SuperAgent description.
- Renamed the Settings sidebar entry to “Tool Add-Ons” to match the add-on management pane.
- Reworked the ROM Builder Resource Monitor card to show live in-app CPU load, memory, disk, host, and refresh-time metrics rather than opening a separate desktop terminal.
- Restored the original ROM Builder Resource Monitor workflow using `btop`, with `bpytop` fallback in a desktop terminal.
- Fixed ROM Builder job status polling and cancellation to use the stable job collection endpoint.
- Fixed Add-On repository discovery to scan ZIP packages in the `PizzaG/A-Team_Agent` `modules` branch tree and download by repository-relative path.
- Improved Android source preflight validation, loaded A-Team setup configuration, and ensured build commands run from the selected ROM source root before sourcing `build/envsetup.sh`.
- Made optional APN assets non-fatal when unavailable, with a clear warning.
- Restored the original ROM Builder resource-monitor launcher, using `btop` with `bpytop` fallback when installed.
- Corrected ROM Builder build execution to run from the selected Android source tree before sourcing `build/envsetup.sh` and invoking build commands.
- Fixed Tool Add-Ons repository defaults to `PizzaG/A-Team_Agent` on the `modules` branch and detect installed modules by their folders, even when they do not contain a manifest.
- Protected the built-in ROM Builder folder from removal through Tool Add-Ons and retained ZIP path validation for downloaded modules.
- Expanded Build Console to span the full width when shown side by side with the configuration pane.
- Improved ROM Builder job execution logs to record the actual working directory used by each action.
- Fixed ROM Builder job-status routing and added clearer persistent job diagnostics.
- Added CPU/GPU temperature, load, and fan telemetry where supported by host sensors.
- Added the Agent Add-Ons ZIP browser with archive-path validation, install, and removal.
- Expanded the language selector and added locale fallbacks for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Russian, with ROM Builder translations for common controls.
- Added ROM Builder source-tree preflight checks and relocated configuration actions into the configuration pane.
- Defaulted enabled reasoning effort to Medium when no explicit preference is set and the selected model supports it.
- Removed the ROM Builder addon's `updates/` directory without changing the Agent updater.
- Added native Browse folder selection for Android source paths while retaining manual path entry.
- Added `logs/addon-rom-builder.log` diagnostics and stable persisted job state under `logs/rom-builder-state`.
- Added a Load Configuration action and ensured Build Console follows Build Configuration in stacked layouts.
- Fixed centering and focus for Add Model and Add Sub-Agent dialogs; renamed the sidebar section to Add-on Tools.
- Aligned App Transparency sliders side by side and fixed optional ROM Builder API routing.
- Added “Build Android ROMs” to the landing-page rotating phrases and reduced “What’s New in A-Team Agent” card sizes.
- Moved the complete ROM Builder operating skill into the ROM-Builder module package; module installation publishes it to DeerFlow's public skills directory and module removal unpublishes it, so its trigger phrases are unavailable while the module is not installed.
- Expanded ROM Builder skill guidance with UI/CLI operation, configuration, task state, shell sessions, logs, destructive-action confirmation, troubleshooting, resource interpretation, and safe build-operator practices.
- Kept the Build Console completion prompt user-driven: after completion it displays two blank lines and “Press ENTER to Exit”; Enter is forwarded to the persistent shell in the loaded ROM source directory, with no automatic directory change.
- Added Ollama's native per-GPU scheduler overhead setting (`OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD=419430400`) when Ollama is started by the A-Team launcher; the Resource Monitor now distinguishes an active Ollama scheduler reserve from monitor-only accounting when an existing or remote daemon is used.
- Improved AMD GPU naming by preferring the kernel DRM product name or ROCm marketing name before falling back to the PCI database description.
- Regrouped the existing Resource Monitor metrics into CPU/RAM and GPU/VRAM sections without adding or removing metrics; made the Custom APN and Use ccache controls the same compact width.
- ROM Builder terminal completion is task-aware: Build ROM returns directly to the source-root shell, while other tasks retain the double-line “Press ENTER to Exit” prompt.
- Ollama GPU spillover policy now configures `LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET=1824` MiB (800 MiB user reserve plus 1 GiB fit headroom) alongside `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD`, addressing llama-server runners that do not apply the scheduler overhead to layer placement.
- ROM Builder Resource Monitor aligns CPU and GPU device names in the same header row.
- ROM Builder Agent skill now has explicit trigger metadata and deterministic lead-prompt routing for “ROM-Builder”, “ROM Builder”, “rom builder”, and “build a rom”; module installation publishes the bundled skill and uninstall removes it.
- Build Configuration controls reordered into the requested three-column, four-row layout; action buttons remain unchanged.
